title: BOCW Punjab 2026: Labour Card, Benefits, Status Check
meta_description: BOCW Punjab 2026: Construction worker labour card benefits, scholarships, maternity, death benefit. Register, check status & download at bocw.punjab.gov.in.

hero.one_liner: BOCW Punjab labour card gives construction workers scholarships, maternity benefit, and death cover. Eligibility, registration, status check, and card download.

what_is_it: BOCW stands for Building and Other Construction Workers. The Punjab Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board is a statutory body under the Punjab government that registers construction workers and provides them with welfare benefits through a labour card.

The BOCW Punjab labour card is a registration card issued to construction workers who meet the eligibility criteria and register with the board. Once registered, the worker and their family become eligible for a range of benefits including education scholarships for children, maternity benefits, financial aid for daughters' marriages, death and disability compensation, and more.

eligibility.label: Days worked
eligibility.value: At least 90 days of construction work in Punjab in the preceding 12 months.

eligibility.label: Income
eligibility.value: Monthly income not more than Rs 15,000.

eligibility.label: Exclusions
eligibility.value: Not a member of EPF, NPS, or ESIC; not an income tax payer.

eligibility.label: Residency
eligibility.value: Working in Punjab; migrant workers from other states can register.

eligibility_filters.notes: Construction worker 18-60, 90 days work in Punjab in last 12 months, monthly income under Rs 15,000, not under EPF/NPS/ESIC.

how_to_apply.title: Check eligibility before applying
how_to_apply.description: Confirm you meet all three core requirements: you are a construction worker aged 18 to 60 years, you have worked in the construction sector in Punjab for at least 90 days in the preceding 12 months, and your monthly income does not exceed ₹15,000. You must also not be a member of EPF (Employees' Provident Fund), NPS, or ESIC.

how_to_apply.title: Visit bocw.punjab.gov.in or a Sewa Kendra
how_to_apply.description: Go to the official BOCW Punjab portal at bocw.punjab.gov.in and click on Worker Registration. Alternatively, visit your nearest Sewa Kendra, the operator will help you complete the registration using the same portal. Online registration is faster, but Sewa Kendra is helpful if you have difficulty uploading documents.

how_to_apply.title: Fill the registration form
how_to_apply.description: Enter your personal details (name, Aadhaar, date of birth, address), employment details (type of construction work, employer or work site, duration of employment), and bank account details. Enter the bank account number and IFSC code carefully, this is where your benefit payments will be sent.

how_to_apply.title: Upload required documents
how_to_apply.description: Upload scanned copies of: Aadhaar card, proof of 90 days of construction work (employer certificate, or a certificate from a contractor or registered trade union confirming 90 days of construction employment in the past 12 months), photograph, and bank passbook. The 90-day proof is the most common bottleneck, get it from your employer or contractor before applying.

how_to_apply.title: Pay the registration contribution
how_to_apply.description: A nominal annual registration contribution is required from the worker. Pay it online through the portal at the time of registration. The exact current fee is listed on bocw.punjab.gov.in, verify before applying as the amount may be updated. After payment confirmation, your registration application is submitted and moves into the Labour Department verification queue. You will receive an SMS confirmation on your registered mobile number once payment is accepted.

how_to_apply.title: Receive your BOCW card
how_to_apply.description: After verification, the BOCW Punjab labour card is generated. You can download and print it from the portal using your registration number. The card shows your name, registration number, validity period, and photograph. Renew the card annually before it expires to maintain continuous access to all benefits.

ministry: Punjab Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board, Labour Department

extra_sections.heading: What Is the BOCW Punjab Labour Card
content: The board operates under the Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1996, and the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Cess Act, 1996. These central laws mandate that states set up welfare boards for construction workers funded by a cess collected from construction projects.

The bocw punjab portal at bocw.punjab.gov.in is the central hub for all registrations, benefit applications, status checks, and card downloads. Workers can register online through the portal or visit their nearest Sewa Kendra or Labour Department office for assisted registration.
For a rejected application, delayed payment, or wrong card details, the Labour Department district office and the BOCW helpline handle grievances. The board has its head office in Chandigarh.

extra_sections.heading: Who Runs It and How It Is Funded
content: The Punjab BOCW board is funded by a 1% cess levied on construction projects with a cost above a certain threshold. This cess is paid by builders and developers to the state government, which transfers it to the welfare board.
The board then uses this fund to run all its welfare schemes. This means the benefits for construction workers are essentially funded by the construction industry itself, not by general taxation.
Most payment failures trace back to a dormant bank account or a broken Aadhaar link rather than a rejected claim. Keep the account active and your mobile number current.

extra_sections.heading: Eligibility in Detail
content: Registration is not automatic. A construction worker in Punjab must actively apply to get the BOCW card.

Many eligible workers in Punjab are unregistered and therefore missing out on benefits they legally qualify for. If you or a family member works in construction, brick laying, plastering, painting, plumbing, electrical work at construction sites, carpentry, stone cutting, or any other activity at a building site, registration is worth pursuing.

Construction work in Punjab covers a wide range of activities. Workers who qualify for BOCW registration include: masons, plumbers, electricians (working at construction sites), painters, carpenters, scaffolders, welders working on building construction, road construction labourers, dam and irrigation project workers, tunnel workers, and even workers involved in demolition.
If your work is at a construction site, you likely qualify regardless of the specific trade.

qualify: 90 days construction work in Punjab in last 12 months
Both spouses can register separately if both work in construction
disqualify: Member of EPF, NPS, or ESIC
Cannot show 90 days of construction work

extra_sections.heading: Other BOCW Schemes Worth Knowing
content: Beyond the main benefits, the board runs an LTC scheme, an occupational-diseases scheme, and reimbursement for spectacles, dental care, and hearing devices. A bicycle scheme also covers workers' children in Classes 9 to 12.
Each of these has its own application within the portal. A registered worker does not get them automatically, so apply per scheme as the need arises.
The cess that funds the board is a 1 percent levy on construction projects above a set cost. This is paid by builders, not by the workers themselves.

extra_sections.title: The 90-Day Proof Is the Biggest Hurdle
extra_sections.content:
The single biggest reason workers fail to register is the 90-day work proof. Workers with years of experience cannot always get a formal employer certificate.

A contractor or registered trade union certificate also works. If neither is available, a self-declaration with two witnesses may be accepted, so verify the current rule at your Labour office.

extra_sections.heading: Who Counts as a Construction Worker
content: Migrant construction workers who work in Punjab but are originally from another state can register with the Punjab BOCW board as long as they can show 90 days of construction work in Punjab in the preceding 12 months. They must have a Punjab address for the registration purpose, typically where they are living and working.
Migrant workers from UP, Bihar, Rajasthan, or other states working at Punjab construction sites are eligible on the same terms as local workers.

extra_sections.heading: How to Register for the Labour Card

steps.title: Check eligibility
steps.desc: Confirm you are 18 to 60, have 90 days of construction work in the last 12 months, earn under Rs 15,000 a month, and are not under EPF, NPS, or ESIC.

steps.title: Get 90-day proof
steps.desc: A Form 28 certificate from your employer or contractor, or a registered trade union certificate, proving 90 days of construction work.

steps.title: Apply on the portal
steps.desc: Register at bocw.punjab.gov.in with Aadhaar and mobile, fill the form, add a nominee, and upload documents and bank details.

steps.title: Get the labour card
steps.desc: After verification the BOCW labour card is issued. Renew it each year by confirming you are still working in construction.

extra_sections.heading: Why Registration and Renewal Matter
content: The labour card has a one-year registration period and must be renewed to keep benefits active. Renewal confirms you are still working in construction.
The board audits its database and removes workers who have left construction. Keep your contribution and details current so your claims are not blocked at the verification stage.

items.title: Education stipend
items.sub: Rs 3,000 to Rs 70,000 a year for a worker's children from Class 1 to degree. The earlier two-year wait has been abolished, so claim from day one.

items.title: Maternity benefit
items.sub: Rs 21,000 per birth for a female worker, Rs 5,000 for a male worker, for up to two children.

items.title: Balri Tohfa Yojana
items.sub: An FDR of Rs 51,000 in a girl child's name, up to two girls, encashable at her marriage.

items.title: Tool kit and pension
items.sub: A one-time tool grant for the worker's trade, plus pension after age 60 for long-registered workers.

extra_sections.heading: The Death and Disability Benefits
content: For the Ex-gratia and Death Benefit schemes, the application is made by the worker's nominee or family member after the accident or death event. These applications require police FIR copies, medical reports, death certificate (in case of death), and the labour card of the deceased or injured worker.
These claims may take longer to process because they involve investigation by the board.

If a worker dies while the BOCW card is active, the nominee (usually the spouse or a child) can claim the ex-gratia and funeral benefit. The nominee should be registered at the time of the worker's initial registration or during renewal.
Always ensure your nominee details are updated and correct, a nominee who is not on record may face delays in claiming death benefits.

extra_sections.title: Accidental Death and Disability Cover
extra_sections.desc:
The nominee gets Rs 5 lakh for accidental death or 100 percent disability, and Rs 3 lakh for natural death.

Funeral assistance of Rs 20,000 is also paid. The claim is filed by the nominee with the death or disability certificate and the labour card number.

extra_sections.heading: Education and Maternity Benefits
content: For the Stipend Scheme (education scholarship), apply at the start of each academic year. You need your child's name, class, school or college name and address, and the fee receipt or enrolment certificate for the year.
The stipend ranges from ₹3,000 per year for Class 1 students up to ₹70,000 per year for degree or professional course students. Verification is done by the board after submission.
For the Maternity Benefit scheme, apply after the delivery, the application requires the child's birth certificate. Female workers receive ₹21,000 for up to two children.
Male workers (claiming on behalf of their wife's delivery) receive ₹5,000. Both applications go through the BOCW portal and the payment goes to the registered worker's bank account via DBT.

extra_sections.title: No More Two-Year Wait for the Stipend
extra_sections.content:
The board abolished the old two-year service condition for the education stipend. You can claim your child's scholarship from the first day of contribution.

Many families held back thinking they had to wait. If your child is in school or college and you are registered, apply now.

extra_sections.heading: Checking Your Application Online
content: To check your bocw status check punjab, go to bocw.punjab.gov.in and look for the 'Check Status' or 'Track Application' section. Enter your registration number or Aadhaar number to see the current status of your registration, renewal, or benefit application.
For bocw card download punjab, log in to bocw.punjab.gov.in with your credentials. Navigate to your profile or card section.
Your BOCW labour card is available as a downloadable PDF. Print it and keep a physical copy, many benefit applications require you to submit a copy of the card.

items.title: Check status
items.sub: Go to bocw.punjab.gov.in, open Check Status or Trace Application, and enter your Aadhaar or registration number with your mobile.

items.title: Download the card
items.sub: Log in with your credentials and download the labour card from your profile or card section as a PDF.

items.title: Forgot login
items.sub: If you cannot log in, visit your nearest Labour Department office with your Aadhaar and registration details to reset access.

items.title: Per-scheme applications
items.sub: Each benefit has its own form within the portal. Apply per scheme after logging in, not all at once.

extra_sections.heading: Applying for Each Benefit
content: Each BOCW welfare scheme has its own application process within the portal. After logging in to bocw.punjab.gov.in with your labour card credentials, go to the 'Apply for Benefits' section and select the specific scheme you are claiming.
Do not try to claim all benefits in one application, each is separate.

For individual benefit applications (stipend, maternity, Balri Tohfa, etc.), each scheme has its own application form within the portal. After logging in, navigate to 'Apply for Benefits' and select the specific scheme.
Fill in the details specific to that benefit, for stipend it's the child's school details and academic year; for maternity it's the delivery date and child's birth certificate.

items.title: Stipend
items.sub: Apply at the start of each academic year with your child's class, school, and fee details.

items.title: Maternity
items.sub: Apply after the delivery with the child's birth certificate. Female workers get the higher Rs 21,000.

items.title: Balri Tohfa
items.sub: Apply after a daughter's birth. The board issues the Rs 51,000 FDR encashable at her marriage.

items.title: Death and ex-gratia
items.sub: Filed by the nominee after the event with the death or accident certificate and the labour card.

extra_sections.heading: Renewal and Keeping Details Updated
content: The BOCW Punjab board periodically holds registration camps in different districts to bring more unregistered construction workers into the system. These camps are announced through the Labour Department and on bocw.punjab.gov.in.
Attending a camp is the fastest route to registration for workers who have difficulty with the online process.

The BOCW card has a registration period, typically one year, after which it must be renewed. Renewal requires confirmation that the worker is still in construction work and payment of the renewal contribution.
Expired registrations lose access to benefits, so timely renewal is important.

extra_sections.text: The single biggest reason construction workers fail to register for BOCW is the 90-day proof requirement. Workers who have genuinely worked in construction for years cannot always produce a formal employer certificate. A certificate from a contractor or a registered trade union confirming 90 days of construction employment is also accepted. If neither is available, a self-declaration supported by two witnesses who can attest to the work history can be submitted with the application, verify this option at your nearest Labour Department office.

extra_sections.heading: Migrant Workers and Both Spouses
content: Families where both husband and wife work in construction can both register separately with the BOCW board. Each worker gets their own card and their own benefit eligibility.

For maternity benefits, a female construction worker who is herself registered gets ₹21,000 for the birth of each child (up to two). Her husband, if also separately registered, gets ₹5,000 for the same birth.
Both claims can be filed simultaneously for the same birth event.

faqs.question: What is the BOCW Punjab labour card and who can get it?
faqs.answer:
The BOCW Punjab labour card is a welfare registration card issued by the Punjab Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. Construction workers aged 18-60 who have worked in Punjab's construction sector for 90 days in the past year, earn ≤₹15,000/month, and are not EPF/NPS/ESIC members are eligible.

The card provides access to scholarships, maternity benefits, compensation, and more.

faqs.question: How to do bocw status check punjab?
faqs.answer:
Go to bocw.punjab.gov.in and look for the Check Status or Track Application section. Enter your registration number or Aadhaar number to see the current status of your registration or benefit application.

You can also log in with your credentials to see more detailed status information for each benefit you have applied for.

faqs.question: How to do bocw card download punjab?
faqs.answer:
Log in to bocw.punjab.gov.in with your registration number and password. Navigate to your profile or card section.

Your BOCW Punjab labour card is available as a downloadable PDF. Download and print it for use in benefit applications.

If you cannot log in, visit your nearest Sewa Kendra or Labour Department office with your Aadhaar.

faqs.question: What benefits does the BOCW Punjab card provide?
faqs.answer: Key benefits include: education stipend for children from Class 1 to degree level (₹3,000-₹70,000/year), maternity benefit (₹21,000 for female workers, ₹5,000 for male workers per child, up to 2 children), Balri Tohfa ₹51,000 FDR for each girl child born (up to 2), Shagun Yojana for daughter's marriage, ex-gratia for accidental death or disability, funeral rites, tool kit, and LTC. Verify current amounts at bocw.punjab.gov.in.

faqs.question: What is the punjab bocw list and how to check if I am registered?
faqs.answer:
The Punjab BOCW list is the list of registered construction workers maintained by the board. Log in to bocw.punjab.gov.in or use the search function to check if your name and registration are active.

You can search by name, registration number, or Aadhaar. Your registration status will show as active, expired, or pending renewal.

faqs.question: How to prove 90 days of construction work for BOCW registration?
faqs.answer:
You need a certificate from your employer, contractor, or a registered trade union confirming 90 days of construction work in Punjab in the last 12 months. If a formal certificate is not available, check with your nearest Labour Department office about whether a self-declaration supported by witnesses is accepted in your district.

The Sewa Kendra operator can also advise on this.

faqs.question: Can a construction worker earning more than ₹15,000 per month register for BOCW Punjab?
faqs.answer:
No. The monthly income limit for BOCW Punjab registration is ₹15,000. Workers earning above this limit are not eligible for the labour card and its associated welfare benefits.

The scheme is targeted at low-income construction workers. If your income fluctuates and is sometimes above and sometimes below this limit, the limit applies to your regular or average monthly earnings.

faqs.question: Do I need to wait two years after BOCW registration to claim the stipend scheme?
faqs.answer:
No. The Punjab BOCW Board abolished the two-year waiting period for the Stipend (education) scheme. You can apply for your child's education scholarship from the very first day of your contribution and registration.

This is a recent change, workers who were told to wait two years under the old rule should recheck and apply immediately.
